what_happened: While reading a request that said everything of Athena's design can be changed, the reader asked Sri whether this should also be stated in the agents' prompts and not just the README. Sri said he didn't know. He didn't expect exact wording to live in the repo and doesn't know the systems well enough to say where a change belongs. He assumed the steward would step back, look at the whole picture, and decide. The question asked him to choose where a change goes inside Athena's design, which is Athena's call.
cause: Nothing tells the reader which questions may go to the user. Placement of a change across docs, prompts and roles is an internal design call. The reader has no rule to settle that itself from the repo, and no check filters out questions the user can't answer before they are asked. The earlier classes cover questions about acceptance methods, policy choices and provenance. None covers a design-placement question that the user has delegated to the steward.
prevention: Add a rule to the reader brief and a code check on its questions. A question to the user must be one only the user can answer: his intent, priorities, or decisions he has reserved. It must not ask where a change belongs among docs, prompts, code or roles. For a request that says Athena's design can be changed, the reader must make the placement call itself. It should cover every surface that governs agent behavior, such as the README, the prompts and the roles, and record the choice in the reading for the steward to check. A request that Athena should know or act on something is treated as a change to agent behavior, not as docs only. The check would flag a reader question that names files, prompts or surfaces as options, and send it back to the reader to resolve.
proposed_request: Make Athena's reader stop asking the customer to choose where a change goes in Athena's design. Outcome: when a request says part of Athena's design can be changed, the reader decides which surfaces need the change (README, agent prompts, roles, working rules) and states that choice in the reading. It asks the customer only questions that depend on his intent, priorities or reserved decisions. Acceptance: (1) the reader's brief says questions to the customer must be answerable only by him and must not offer file, prompt or role placement as the choice; (2) a code check on the reader's questions sends back any question that asks where in the design a change should go, and the reader must resolve it itself; (3) a test replays the question 'Do you want this stated in the agents' prompts too, not just the README?' and shows it is sent back, while a question about the customer's priorities passes; (4) a test shows that a request saying 'everything of its design can be changed' yields a reading that covers both the README and the agent prompts without asking; (5) the changelog has an entry.
